you.snippet:
The announcement from Rockstar Games would mean GTA VI has already earned more than the entire box office run of the highest-grossing film of all time ... Grand Theft Auto VI generated $3.79bn in retail sales on its first day, publisher Rockstar Games has announced, calling it the biggest launch for any entertainment product in history.
The game went on sale Thursday on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, launching first in New Zealand and rolling out market by market as each reached midnight local time. The release quickly became a global phenomenon, generating more social media posts than this year’s World Cup, according to monitoring platform Visibrain. Critics praised the game, which has a score of 99 on review aggregator Metacritic. Rockstar said that made it the highest-rated game ever. Like its predecessors, “GTA VI” is an open-world action game in which players roam freely through a sprawling city, stealing cars, pulling off heists and carrying out missions for criminal gangs.
There is insufficient evidence supporting a scientific causal link between violent video games and violent behaviour, according to the American Psycyhological Association. Nonetheless, several police departments took to the internet with warnings – and even jokes – aimed at keeping GTA VI’s lawlessness firmly in the virtual world.
“GTA is not a real place, but Atlanta is!” the department warned.
